title: BlueSense
tagline: Predict water risk, protect every drop.
summary: BlueSense is a water-intelligence and decision-support prototype for Bangladesh. It joins ERA5 weather, FAO AQUASTAT statistics and GRACE satellite storage in one workspace. It forecasts each division's water balance 1–6 months ahead with Random Forest models (90% intervals, SHAP), tests what-if scenarios, balances and optimises a water budget, and plans irrigation with FAO-56. A grounded AI Copilot answers only through 15 read-only tools and cites the project's own documents. Every number shows its source and date.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body:
Bangladesh plans water use on information that is **scattered, mixed in time and hard to turn into decisions**.

- **Scattered.** Weather reanalysis, forecasts, FAO national statistics and satellite water-storage data sit in separate portals and formats.
- **Mixed in time and space.** National withdrawal statistics date from 2008 and resource figures from 2018, weather comes from point data, and GRACE resolves about 300 km. These are easy to misread as current, local measurements.
- **Hard to act on.** Turning weather into crop water need (FAO-56), or testing "what if rainfall falls 20%?", needs models most advisers cannot run.
- **Risky with generic AI.** A chatbot can invent numbers or present a simulation as a fact.

The stakes are real:
- In the latest FAO AQUASTAT record (2008), agriculture took **87.8%** of withdrawals (31.5 of 35.87 km³/yr), and **79%** of all withdrawals came from groundwater.
- The national GRACE storage trend is **−0.53 cm/yr** for 2002–2026.

> The user problem is a *proposed* problem with a *hypothetical* persona (an extension adviser in Rajshahi). It has not been validated with customer research yet.

sections.title: Solution
sections.body:
**BlueSense** is one web workspace that turns public water data into decisions, with the source and date beside every number.

- **Monitor:** Command Center KPIs, alerts, a division map and the Water Rhythm timeline.
- **Predict:** Random Forest forecasts of the monthly climatic water balance (P − ET0), 1, 3 and 6 months ahead, with 90% intervals and SHAP explanations.
- **Simulate:** a What-if simulator with seven levers, a balanced water budget (Sankey), an LP allocation optimiser and a conceptual 3D distribution network.
- **Recommend:** Smart Irrigation (FAO-56) gives the next irrigation date and volume, with every input listed.
- **Explain:** an AI Copilot that answers only through 15 read-only tools. It cites the project's own method documents (RAG) and flags any number it cannot verify.

BlueSense is decision support. It does not replace field monitoring, laboratory testing or government systems.

sections.title: Why Now
sections.body:
- **Open data has matured.** ERA5 reanalysis and forecasts (Open-Meteo), GRACE/GRACE-FO storage (2002–2026) and FAO AQUASTAT are freely available through APIs.
- **AI can now be grounded.** LLMs with tool calling and retrieval can answer from a system's own data and documents instead of from memory. BlueSense uses this to keep answers checkable.
- **Low cost to run.** The whole stack runs on free tiers: Vercel hosting, the Gemini free tier, Open-Meteo, and n8n for automation. A pilot needs no hardware.
- **The water-storage signal is moving.** GRACE shows a long-term national decline (−0.53 cm/yr), while farms keep relying on stored water in the dry season.

sections.title: Product Demo
sections.body:
**Try it:** [the live app](https://blue-sense.vercel.app). The Copilot answers on the live link; the 2:54 pitch video link will be added here once it is uploaded.

A 6-step journey through the working prototype:

1. **Command Center → Rajshahi:** KPIs with source and date, alerts, and the division map. Replay rainfall anomalies in **Water Rhythm**.
2. **What-if:** apply "Dry year: rainfall −20%" and compare baseline vs simulated stress and unmet demand.
3. **Water Budget:** check that the balance closes, then run the optimiser.
4. **Prediction Lab:** read the 1/3/6-month forecast, its interval, test metrics against baselines, and SHAP.
5. **Smart Irrigation:** get the next irrigation date and volume, with a "why" list.
6. **AI Copilot:** ask "How is the forecast made?". It calls `search_docs` and cites `[MODEL_CARD.md > Models]`.

The 3D Water Flow module is a **conceptual simulation** on a hypothetical network and is labelled as such.

sections.title: Market Opportunity
Business Model
sections.body:
These are hypotheses to test, not results:

- **Institutional pilot → hosted service** for advisory or planning teams, with training and support.
- **Education licence:** BlueSense as a teaching tool, since every equation and parameter is exposed.
- **Custom deployments:** adding a partner's own station data through the existing BWDB importer.

Every option must respect the source licences; the non-commercial terms on some inputs are a known constraint. There is no revenue today.

sections.title: Traction
Competition
Unique Advantage
sections.body:
1. **Provenance on every value.** A first-class `Measure` type carries unit, data kind, source, observation and retrieval dates, spatial level and freshness, across all 45 API operations.
2. **One calculation path.** The UI, the Copilot and the MCP server call the same functions, so they always show the same numbers.
3. **Honest ML.** Chronological splits, two baselines, measured interval coverage, SHAP, and a model card that states its weak points.
4. **Grounded AI.** 15 read-only tools, hybrid RAG with citations, a number check, and no canned or invented answers.
5. **Bangladesh-specific modelling.** Transboundary inflow shaped by GloFAS, Boro/Aman/Aus rice with AWD advice, Bangla names, and Bangla Copilot replies.

sections.title: Go-To-Market
sections.body:
**Proposed pilot plan:**
1. Observe one real planning or advisory workflow and pick one decision BlueSense supports, for example dry-season irrigation timing.
2. Run a side-by-side exercise: the current method vs BlueSense.
3. Measure task completion, time to find the right source and date, understanding of uncertainty, and error reports.
4. Iterate, then offer a supervised pilot to an advisory team and a university course.

**Channels:** agricultural extension networks, university water and climate programmes, and competition and incubator showcases.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.body:
A **modular monolith**: one Next.js frontend and one FastAPI backend, with layered routers, services and pure engines over SQLite. An offline ML pipeline produces model artifacts. The Copilot reaches Gemini only from the server.

- **Shared tool registry:** the MCP server reuses the Copilot's tools.
- **n8n:** calls the public API on a schedule.
- **Live hosting:** both apps are on Vercel. The backend runs a checksum-verified, read-only database snapshot.

sections.title: Technology Stack
sections.body:
| Layer | Technologies |
|---|---|
| Frontend | Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Zustand, Plotly, D3 + d3-sankey, MapLibre GL, React Three Fiber |
| Backend | Python, FastAPI, Pydantic 2, pandas, NumPy, SciPy (HiGHS LP), httpx, APScheduler |
| Database | SQLite (WAL, 8 checksummed migrations, verified backups); live: read-only seed |
| AI / ML | scikit-learn Random Forest (selected over XGBoost), SHAP, Google Gemini (Copilot), `gemini-embedding-2` + BM25 (RAG), MCP Python SDK |
| Automation | n8n Cloud (Schedule, HTTP, Code, Gmail) |
| Infra | Vercel (frontend, and backend as a Preview upload behind a stable alias); Docker/Render blueprint kept for self-hosting |
| Quality | pytest, Ruff, ESLint, `tsc`, Vitest, Playwright + axe |

sections.title: API Documentation
Data Layer
sections.body:
| Source | What | Coverage in the repository |
|---|---|---|
| Open-Meteo (ERA5/ERA5-Land) | Daily rain, temperature, FAO-56 ET0, soil moisture at 8 division points | 1991-01-01 → 2026-11-05 (104,744 rows) |
| FAO AQUASTAT | Renewable resources, withdrawals, irrigated area, SDG 6.4.2 | 25 indicators; reference years 2008/2018 kept |
| CSR GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06.3 | Terrestrial water storage anomaly | 2002-04 → 2026-09 (259 months) |
| geoBoundaries, HDX, World Bank | Boundaries, population 2022, projection to 2050 | Static |

**Processing:** validated adapters with retries. Missing or out-of-range values are never stored and never overwrite stored data. Monthly values use complete months only.

**Storage:** SQLite with 25 tables. Every record keeps its source and retrieval time.

**Privacy:**
- no personal data is collected and there are no accounts;
- Copilot questions go to Google Gemini (free tier: Google may use them; disclosed in the app);
- logs hash the client id and never store message text.

sections.title: AI Layer
Product Roadmap
Performance & Scalability
sections.body:
**Today:** a single backend instance over SQLite (WAL) with read-only connections and GZip.
- Cache headers: 60 s for current and forecast data, 300 s otherwise.
- The frontend keeps a 5-minute request cache.
- Heavy visuals load lazily, and maps fall back to SVG without WebGL.

**Limits:** SQLite and in-memory Copilot limits suit one instance. The live backend is a read-only snapshot, and Vercel functions on the current plan allow up to 300 s per request; the Copilot has a 240 s deadline.

**To scale:** move to a managed database with a shared rate-limit store, run sync jobs separately, and add CDN caching for read-heavy endpoints.
